rationale: The accruals × net-equity-issuance pairing is close to the well-documented net external financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan), but the second-difference (acceleration) framing of the accrual gap is a genuine refinement and the rank-product direction is consistent with the negative expected sign.

The two legs are mechanically offsetting — wcap = act − lct and lct includes dlc, so growth in short-term debt directly depresses Δwcap — making the MIN of the two ranks internally inconsistent with the stated "build funded by short-term debt" story, on top of Δwcap/at being the textbook Sloan working-capital accrual.

Sign error: recch and invch are cash-flow-statement items signed as cash impact (a receivable/inventory *increase* enters negative), so high RANK(ADD(recch,invch)) selects firms *liquidating* working capital, the opposite of the hypothesized build, inverting the intended interaction.

The ABS in the denominator discards the sign of operating cash flow (so cash-burning and cash-generating firms with the same |oancf| rank identically) and creates explosive values for near-zero OCF, and the underlying accruals × external-financing construct largely duplicates proposal 1 without adding an independent mechanism.

Essentially the mirror image of the known accruals-plus-net-external-financing composite, but the construction is internally coherent (both legs ranked so that high = clean accruals and net capital return, matching the positive sign) and the 3-year accrual smoothing is a defensible persistence refinement.

The INDICATOR gate assigns 0 to all firms with non-rising accrual trends, pooling heavy diluters in the "off" state with non-diluters in the "on" state at the same signal value, which corrupts both tails of the sort; the 5-year trend window also erodes coverage on top of a signal whose core is the well-known net share issuance anomaly.
